rationale: All spec criteria are satisfied and all three review lenses ran successfully. One major finding: delete_all_executions_by_workflow_id now issues N+1 Conversation.exists() queries — one new DB roundtrip per execution with a conversation_id — rather than a single batched IN query. For workflows with many executions this can saturate the connection pool. The fix is a small targeted change. No security, breaking-change, or public-API concerns found. Commit format and code quality gates pass.

findings.title: N+1 DB queries in delete_all_executions_by_workflow_id
findings.problem: delete_all_executions_by_workflow_id now calls Conversation.exists() once per execution that has a non-null conversation_id. Each call opens a new SQLAlchemy Session and issues a separate SELECT against the conversations table.
findings.impact: The DELETE /workflows/{workflow_id}/executions endpoint and the workflow deletion path call this method without a user filter. A workflow with hundreds of executions (common for automated or scheduled workflows) will fire hundreds of individual Conversation.exists() queries, each acquiring a DB connection. Under load this can saturate the connection pool and cause latency spikes.
findings.recommendation: Batch the existence check: collect all non-null conversation_ids from the fetched executions, issue a single SELECT id FROM conversations WHERE id IN (...), build a set of existing ids, then filter the deletion loop from that set. This reduces N+1 to 2 queries regardless of execution count.
